title: AI Agents for Performance: Ship Faster, Pay Less — Rajat Shah, Netflix
talk_summary: Rajat Shah describes using coding agents to read profiler output, locate hot code at the production commit, propose fixes, and validate them with tests/canary before human review. The core reusable mechanism is a centralized Git catalog of performance patterns/anti-patterns that shifts detection from reactive profiling to review-time and authoring-time checks.

takeaways.what_they_do: They keep a central, human- and agent-readable Git repo of patterns/anti-patterns with symbols, affected services, and confidence; agents query it instead of rediscovering issues.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can start with just a markdown files in a in a centralized Git repo.

takeaways.what_they_do: The agent runs unit/integration tests, then a canary comparing old vs new code on CPU, latency, and error rate; it opens a PR only if the report is positive.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Profiler gives the estimate, canary gives ground truth.

takeaways.technique: Fixed level-2 workflow with scheduled runs
takeaways.what_they_do: They use a predefined workflow: trigger profile, download data, analyze, run canary, suggest fix; then schedule it weekly per service.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you could essentially have a scheduled run on your services every week

takeaways.what_they_do: Reviewer agents look up the catalog and leave inline comments on likely anti-patterns; coding agents can also consult it before writing code.

takeaways.technique: Hierarchical indexed catalog to avoid context bloat
takeaways.what_they_do: They structure the catalog so agents navigate to exact entries rather than dumping the whole catalog into context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: doesn't fill up the agent context too much, but rather it can navigate it in a very hierarchical format

takeaways.technique: Structured profiler/observability data as agent input
takeaways.what_they_do: They feed profiler call-stack data with self/inclusive CPU to an LLM, which maps hot methods to the production commit and traces the call path.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the output of a profiling data is actually very similar and very well-structured for an LLM agent to use.
takeaways.numbers: 8.8% CPU; under 5 minutes; seven services; 0.5-4.6% CPU savings
